precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. We are the ones being justified. Not all nations on the planet. Paul is not saying everybody on the planet is going to be justified. Nope. He is getting that from what we are reading right there.
precepts.point: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. He shall be glorified in his Son.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified”. Here is that word again, predestinate. And who is justified? Isaiah: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

We are the ones being justified, not all nations on the planet. Paul is not saying everybody on the planet is going to be justified. He did not make things up and pull them out of the sky; he is getting that from what Isaiah wrote.

“and whom he justified, them he also glorified”. The seed of Israel justified in the Lord “shall glory”, and he shall be glorified in his Son.

That is why Paul goes on: “If God be for us, who can be against us?” Who can conquer us, who can destroy us? Nobody on this planet, no matter what comes our way. The seed of Israel, called and justified in the Lord, are more than conquerors through him that loved us, and nothing shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect. So there's no contradiction from the New Testament and the Old Testament; the contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors.
precepts.point: I will seek that which was lost: that's our people. And bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken: we were broken. And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Who are the elect the angels gather in Matthew 24? Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name.” Israel is God's elect.

So there's no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old Testament. Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the angels gather the elect, and the elect is Israel. Ezekiel's sheep, Matthew's elect and Isaiah's elect are the same people.

The contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors, who tell the people it is everybody. The Lord said: “I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick.” That's our people: we were broken, we're the sick ones. “but I will destroy the fat and the strong”: he is going to destroy the nations. “I will feed them with judgment.”

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect. That is who the elect of God is.
precepts.point: The Lord through the apostle Paul is instructing the Colossians on how to deal with one another: bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering, forbearing one another and forgiving one another. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, so there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
In verse 11 Paul references us as the Greeks, the Barbarians and the Scythians. Then in verse 12 he says it one more time, plainly: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God”. He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathens to understand. Isaiah tells us who the elect of God is: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”.

Israel is his elect. So the elect of God that Paul is instructing in Colossians 3:12 are Israelites.

They know good and well this Bible don’t belong to them. But in slavery they played on our ignorance. We couldn’t read or write; they taught it to us by oral tradition, wouldn’t let us read the Bible, and gave us the slave Bible where the majority of the Bible wasn’t even there. They wanted to keep us docile, ignorant and misinformed. But there is a God, the God of Israel, who has poured his spirit upon his people in these last days, and now we know what the Bible is talking about: Israel mine elect.

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. That justification is for one people. Yes, we became heathen, but we are still going to be justified through Christ.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Galatians says God would “justify the heathen through faith”. Who is that justification for? “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” Shall the seed of what be justified? Israel.

So it is what it is. Yes, we became heathen, following after the heathen in their holidays, their foods and their white image; but we are still going to be justified through Christ, and we shall glory. The justification is for one people, the seed of Israel.

That is why the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israelites and not the slave master's property to be taught his religion. The masters' books called us heathens in need of their instruction, but the Lord had already written that all the seed of Israel, heathen as we became, would be justified in him.

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified. The only ones being justified is all the seed of Israel. It's not talking about the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, all those false religions.
precepts.point: To be conformed to the image of his Son: he's going to transform us, the 12 tribes, into the image of his Son Christ, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“whom he called, them he also justified”. Who is being justified? Isaiah answers: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The only ones being justified are all the seed of Israel. It is not talking about the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, not any of those false religions.

That is why there is predestination in the Bible. People love to say there is no such thing, but there is, for the 12 tribes of Israel. We were his people in the past, we are going to be his people today and forevermore; we are predestined to be his chosen forever. Whether we as individuals make it or not is up to each individual.

And “whom he justified, them he also glorified”: the seed of Israel that is justified in the Lord “shall glory.” The whole chain of Romans 8:29-30, foreknown, predestinated, called, justified and glorified, runs through the seed of Israel, whom God will transform into the image of his Son, Christ, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect. We are the elect. Israel is the elect, not all nations. So this is where Paul's getting that from.
precepts.point: And if by grace, then is it no more of works: now a Christian will try to hem you up with that. See, it's not about works, my brother. Because Christians assume when Paul used the word works, Paul is talking about thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. No, that's not what Paul's talking about at all.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no: God has not cast away the 12 tribes of Israel. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Read that first verse on the street and it tells you what the subject is about.

Paul speaks of “a remnant according to the election of grace.” Who is the elect? Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” We are the elect. Israel is the elect, not all nations. This is where Paul is getting that from.

Paul even says “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew”: there is that word again, the same as Romans 8:29, so we did not even have to go to Amos 3; Paul deals with it here. Elijah thought he was by himself, but God answered, “I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.” The elect remnant is Israel.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. And so, meaning as a result of all that has been said: all 12 tribes shall be saved. “For this is my covenant unto them”: unto the 12 tribes of Israel, the elect of Isaiah 45.

precepts.text: Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus. Why is that important? This was written, write this down, 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people.
precepts.point: Verse three: he makes a proclamation to all 12 tribes. Who is there among you of all his people? He's not just talking to Judah. And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth: if you decide you don't want to go back to the land of Israel, you want to stay where you've been living for all these decades, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts. So some of the northern kingdom did go back with the kingdom of Judah; some of the southern kingdom decided, no, we're going to stay out here too. Everybody did not go back.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
During the Persian captivity we got liberty. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”, and he said that because he knew it was a prophecy. Isaiah had written it: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

Why is that important? Write this down: it was written 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew that the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people. It goes into more detail in the writings of Flavius Josephus, how the prophets showed Cyrus what he must do. And he obeyed.

So he made his proclamation to all twelve tribes: “Who is there among you of all his people?” Not just Judah. And whoever chose to stay where they had been living for decades, “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Some of the northern kingdom went back with Judah; some of the southern kingdom stayed out. Everybody did not go back.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect. The elect are not anybody that worships; the elect is Israel.
precepts.point: He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. Notice the angels do not go to one land to gather this people. Christ is letting us know the Israelites would not be in a land; the Israelites are scattered worldwide.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
People say the people in the land of Israel today are the Jews. That is not what the Bible says. After the tribulation, when the stars fall (the missiles) and the powers of the heavens are shaken (nations warring against each other), “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Notice the angels do not go to one land to gather this people. Christ is letting us know the Israelites would not be in a land; they would be scattered worldwide.

Who is the elect? Some say anybody who worships. Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. That is the elect: Israel, scattered in the four winds from one end of heaven to the other.

Before the angels come for them, the Lord calls to the heavens and to the earth: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” The saints are “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”, and only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. The call to the heavens is to the angels; the call to the earth is to us.

So the message for us on earth is the same as the angels' commandment: gather the saints. We are not supposed to be looking for other races and nationalities, only the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered worldwide, which is why the gospel has to go out to every land.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake and Israel mine elect: we are the elect.
precepts.point: All the tribes of the earth mourn and he sends his angels to gather his elect from the four winds: the elect is Jacob and Israel, not the Baptist church nor all races, and some Israelites who never heard still have to be fetched.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Who is the elect? Not everybody.

Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. We are the elect. Israel is the elect. Not the Baptist church, and not all races on the planet.

And it is from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other, because Isaiah 66 already showed there are Israelites scattered in the isles afar off who have not heard his fame nor seen his glory, and we have to go get them.

Before that gathering, “then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”. It is going to be a happy day, but we will be crying and fearful too. And it comes only after the tribulation. Christ is not returning this year or next year; bad things have to happen first and we have to be proven. Not being able to pay your light bill is not tribulation. We are too comfortable, still smoking weed, going to the club, defiling the Sabbath, the women dressed like hoes with no clothes; in their affliction they will seek him, and the affliction has not even begun.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake and Israel mine elect. The elect gathered from the four winds are the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet and gather his elect from the four winds. Israel is his elect.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
Christ says that after the tribulation of those days, when the stars fall from heaven (the missiles the prophets saw) and the powers of the heavens are shaken, “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Who is the elect?

Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. Israel is the elect. The elect gathered from the four winds are the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered to the ends of the earth.

And notice when it happens. He comes in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory after the tribulation and the war. There is no thought that he might come tomorrow; the tribulation has not come yet, and World War III is already in process. First the war and the shaking of Idumea, the powers of the heavens; then the sign of the Son of man, all the tribes of the earth mourning, and the gathering of Jacob's seed, Israel his elect, out of every nation where they were scattered.

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. Whether called Jews or Gentiles, all the seed of Israel is justified by faith in Christ. Show me one precept where all the seed of Edom, Moab, Ishmael, or Canaan is justified; it is nowhere in the law and prophets.
precepts.point: The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith”. How do we know who is justified? You will not find anywhere in the law and the prophets that Christ was going to justify, atone for or reconcile all the heathen Gentile nations through his death. What you find is this: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

All the seed of Israel, all the families scattered abroad over the earth, justified by faith in Christ. Whether they are called Jews or called Gentiles, they shall be justified, because Christ died for them among the nations.

Now show me a precept where all the seed of Edom will be justified. All the seed of Moab justified. All the seed of Ishmael, all the seed of the Canaanites. Show me one place. It is nowhere in there.

So “they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham”: the Israelites who have faith in Christ are the children of Abraham, known for his strong faith. Abraham believed God first, and only afterward offered sacrifices, and his faith, not the animal, was counted for righteousness. That is how the seed of Israel is justified, and why “they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. Not all the seed of Israel and anybody else, not the good nations, not the individual heathens with black friends. My righteous servant justifies many by dying on the cross for all twelve tribes.
precepts.point: It was not written for his sake alone, but for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead, who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification. Israel was accustomed to sacrificing; Paul says fine, but acknowledge Christ first, because if you put your faith in the animal and the temple falls, you have condemned yourself by default with no animal, no priest, and no temple.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Isaiah 53 says “by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many”. Somebody says, see, many means anybody. Isaiah has something for that: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Not all the seed of Israel and anybody else outside of Israel. Not all the good nations. Not individual heathens who say they have black friends. All the seed of Israel, all twelve tribes, shall be justified.

How? My righteous servant justifies many by dying on the cross, by laying on himself the iniquity of them all. That is the “justification” Paul speaks of when he says Christ “was raised again for our justification”, and it is why Romans 5 opens, “Therefore being justified by faith”. Who, according to the Old Testament, would be justified? Israel.

So when you read justification all throughout Paul’s letters, there should be no confusion about what he is talking about or who he is talking about. Abraham’s faith was imputed to him for righteousness, and “it was not written for his sake alone”, but for his seed who believe on him that raised up Jesus from the dead.

precepts.text: The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans: the three ribs.
precepts.point: The three ribs in its mouth are the three nations Persia conquered: Egypt, Ethiopia, and the Sabeans. This kingdom is very significant for what is happening today.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
The second beast is “like to a bear”, and the bear is the Persians and the Medes. “it raised up itself on one side”: Persia raised itself up, because through King Cyrus, Persia became mightier than Media. “and it had three ribs in the mouth of it between the teeth of it”. What three nations do those ribs represent? Isaiah 45:14 answers: “Thus saith the Lord, The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans”. The three ribs are Egypt, Ethiopia and the Sabeans, the nations Persia conquered.

This kingdom of Persia and Media is very significant for what is going on today. The Achaemenid Empire of Old Persian was an ancient Iranian empire, founded by Cyrus the Great in 550 BC. The bear of Daniel 7 is Iran.

And the Lord worked through that Persian king. “the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.” The Lord spoke to him, and he listened. Isaiah says of him, “He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.” And the chapter of the three ribs opens, “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him”.

So the Lord used King Cyrus, a Persian, to let us go back and build the temple, and gave him Egypt, Ethiopia and the Sabeans to devour. That is why the bear rose up on one side, and why the land of Persia, Iran, stands in prophecy for the days we are in.

precepts.text: Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden to subdue nations before him.
precepts.point: The Lord spoke to a Persian king and he listened, letting us return and build the temple.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Isaiah goes on: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

That is why Cyrus could say, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”. The Lord held his right hand and subdued nations before him. The Lord used King Cyrus, who was a Persian, to allow us to go back and build the temple.

Cyrus is also the one who gave that decree. And the kingdom he ruled, Persia and Media, is Iran today, which is why his story is very significant for what is going on now.

precepts.text: The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over unto thee in chains. The three ribs God promised Cyrus for releasing Israel.
precepts.point: The little horn that came up among them is America, which came out of Britain and plucked up three of the first horns: France, Britain and Spain. Its eyes like the eyes of man are vision, the airplane, the moon landing, the phone, shared with his European brothers and nobody else. Its mouth speaking great things blasphemes the Most High.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
The second beast is “like to a bear, and it raised up itself on one side, and it had three ribs in the mouth of it between the teeth of it”. The bear is Persia and Media, a dual empire, and it raised itself up on one side because Persia rose up greater than the Medes. To explain the three ribs, go to Isaiah 45.

It opens, “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him”. God chose Cyrus the Persian to release the Israelites. And what did Persia receive? “The labour of Egypt”: that is one rib. “and merchandise of Ethiopia”: that is the second. “and of the Sabeans”: that is Somalia, the third. “men of stature”, tall men, “shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall come after thee; in chains they shall come over, and they shall fall down unto thee”.

So when the Most High told Cyrus to release his people from captivity, he promised to make him ruler over many nations, and these three are the ribs between the bear's teeth. “and they said thus unto it, Arise, devour much flesh”: that means conquer. The Scripture explains the Scripture; the ribs are not a mystery once you lay the precept beside the vision.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect.
precepts.point: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God. Isaiah 45:4 says 'Israel mine elect.' The strangers are Israelites.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”, and calls them “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”. Who are the elect? Isaiah answers it: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name”. Israel mine elect, or my chosen, same thing. So the strangers Peter is writing to are Israelites. They are the grafted in strangers, the ones called not a people, not my people, the northern kingdom.

The thought does not change in chapter 2; he is not writing to somebody else. “But ye are a chosen generation”: the “ye” is the strangers of chapter 1 verse 1, the elect of verse 2. Chosen goes back to elect. They are “a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, and all Israel is a peculiar people. Context matters. Against them stand “them which be disobedient”, the builders, the southern kingdom's Pharisees, Sadducees, scribes, elders and rulers, who stumbled at the stone and were appointed to it, so Christ could be killed and die for both kingdoms, to reunite all twelve tribes. That could not be done unless Christ died.

Peter is quoting Hosea. Jezreel is the seed of Israel, and God says “I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people”. So Peter writes “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”. That promise was made to the northern kingdom in Isaiah 7 and 8 and Hosea 1. When Christ dies he redeems them back into being his people and gathers them together in one. How could you find that out if you don't know your history?

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation, world without end. Israel is the world.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Romans 11:12 says “Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles”. The fall of them is the builders, the leaders of the southern kingdom, rejecting Christ, and the diminishing is the same thing in different wording: something that decays, drops lower, falls. What are the riches of the world? Is it talking about money? No: the kingdom. The Pharisees had to reject Christ because it was their lot; Christ had to be killed, and once he died on that cross he granted us access to the kingdom. That is the riches of the world.

And who is the world? Some say, world is Israel, where did you get that from? World is world. No, it's not. The world is us: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” Israel is the world without end.

Christ says the same in Mark 10:30: “in the world to come eternal life.” The world to come is our kingdom, eternal life. That is the riches of the world.

So when Romans 11:15 says “if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world”, it is speaking of Israel. To reconcile is to bring back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us.

precepts.text: Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour. He does not reveal himself to everyone, so if he has shown you who you are, you cannot take it lightly.
precepts.point: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth? The Bible is God's excellent things, not a prosperity tool or a debate about what we feel like doing. He expects excellence, so change your mind to his standard instead of the crumbs society leaves our people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war.
precepts.point: I form the light and create darkness; I make peace and create evil; I the Lord do all these things.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
In Isaiah 45 the Lord says, “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me”. God surnamed us, and even though he revealed himself to us and delivered us numerous times, we kept turning our backs on him. “I am the Lord, and there is none else, there is no God beside me”. Some set themselves up as gods, and some create gods in their minds and as idols, but there is none with him. “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things”.

Exodus 15:3 fills in the picture: “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name”. The same Lord that forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil is also a man of war. That is the overall picture of the Lord our God.

Psalms 46 shows what that looks like: “Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth”. Pharaohs were worshipped as gods, Xerxes thought he was a god, and Antiochus Epiphanes thought he was God manifest on earth; rulers rise in power and rise in pride. But “He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder”. The man on the thumbnail who has claimed for two years that he will stop the war between Ukraine and Russia has not stopped anything. When the Iron Dome in Israel failed and the rockets came through, that was no technical glitch; the Lord ripped it open. He makes the prideful instruments of man fail, because he decides where war happens and when it ceases.

And that God of war, who formed the light and created darkness, is Christ. He is our refuge, and he teaches his soldiers to do the same: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”. He handpicked us to be soldiers in his army.

precepts.text: Israel is called God's elect by name; there is no precept anywhere that calls a nation outside Israel his elect.
precepts.point: After the fishing comes the hunting, out of every mountain and hill and out of the holes of the rock where the nations are hiding, which is not salvation alongside us.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory: that is the justified and glorified of the precept above, with no concordance needed.
precepts.point: You can tell it is not you if you are secretly in adultery or fornication with no repentance, carrying hatred for your brother and disrespecting your spouse; the elect fall and get back up.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Blessed be my rock, and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation: the rock and the God of the rock, the same two as the Holy One and his Maker.
precepts.point: The Father never spoke to anyone on the earth and no one ever heard his voice.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation; salvation is spoken to Israel.
precepts.point: That settles 1 John 2:2 for the Christians who run to it. John was a Jew of the southern kingdom, so our sins means the southern kingdom; and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world means all twelve tribes, the whole world of Israel. Alongside Isaiah 45:17 and John 18:20, Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 is the precept that shows who the whole world is.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
“But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” Salvation is spoken to Israel.

That lines up with the breastplate, where the whole world in the long garment is the twelve tribes of Israel, their names graven in the four rows of stones. When John writes that Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, the everlasting salvation is Israel's, the whole world of the twelve tribes, and not the Moabite, the Jebusite or the Edomite.

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the LORD with an everlasting salvation, world without end; that is the whole world the propitiation covers.
precepts.point: Christ is the advocate and the propitiation, the mercy, for our sins; there is no more Levite priest sacrifice, for he is the mediator between us and the Most High now. The whole world in that verse is the whole world of the nation of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 5: Put Out of the Camp, and the Law of Jealousies

precepts.why:
Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, and Isaiah shows which world that is: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.”

Israel is saved in the Lord, world without end. That is the whole world the propitiation covers: the whole world of the nation of Israel, whose trespass against the Lord is now atoned for through Christ rather than the ram at the priest’s hand.

precepts.text: The Most High forms the light and creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil; I the LORD do all these things.
precepts.point: The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
“I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things.”

The Most High forms the light and creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil. So an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem is no accident and no work of some other power; “I the Lord do all these things.” He is the one who sent it, so that the blood of the seventy sons of Jerubbaal would come back on the man who slew them and the men who aided him.

precepts.text: The Lord speaks to his anointed Cyrus, whose right hand he holds to subdue nations before him.
precepts.point: Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem. His coming was prophesied long before by name.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”. The Lord calls Cyrus his anointed, and holds his right hand to subdue nations before him.

That is how a king of Persia comes to say “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”. The Most High subdued the nations before him and opened the gates, and then stirred up his spirit to make the proclamation. Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him, prophesied by name long before, to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem.

precepts.text: I form the light and create darkness, I make peace and create evil, I the Lord do all these things.
precepts.point: Even then it was the Lord that gave it to you, because the Lord handed you over to Satan; He put that stumbling block before you and you fell over it.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things.” Job understood it: everything that we have comes from the Lord, everything that we get comes from the Lord. So he fell down and worshipped: “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.”

What good is it for us to blame God for stuff that we lose, when he can give it right back to you? There is nothing in this world that you can get yourself without the help of the Lord, unless you serve Satan and he gives it to you, but do you really want to pay that price? Even then it was the Lord that gave it to you, because the Lord handed you over to Satan; he put that stumbling block before you and you fell over it. Peace and evil both come from him, and “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.”

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation and shall not be ashamed nor confounded, world without end.
precepts.point: We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; He put us in captivity for our disobedience. As long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
The psalmist prays, “O let not the oppressed return ashamed: let the poor and needy praise thy name.” The congregation of the poor is the Israelites, and Isaiah gives the answer to that prayer: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.”

Our people will not return to the Lord ashamed. The prophecies show Israel will be redeemed with a mighty salvation, an everlasting salvation, not ashamed nor confounded, world without end. That is the covenant the psalmist asks the Most High to have respect unto: that his people would inherit the Kingdom of Heaven, established from Adam and Shem onward.

We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; he put us in captivity for our disobedience, and the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of cruelty. But as long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting. Israel shall be saved.

precepts.text: Tyre, Zidon, and the coasts of Palestine, the modern-day Arabs of Ishmael, sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem to the Grecians, the white people united under Alexander; God returns their recompense on their own head.
precepts.point: The word "world" means a group of people with common goals or interests, like the sports world or basketball world, so "world without end" and God so loved the world are not speaking of everybody but of Israel.

note.label: Isaiah 45: I Form the Light and Create Darkness

precepts.why:
“The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thine: they shall come after thee; in chains they shall come over”. This is prophecy that the Africans, the men of stature, come over in chains, because they sold us into slavery to the so-called white man, the Grecians. Joel names the sellers: “Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head”.

Tyre, Zidon and the coasts of Palestine are the modern-day Arabs of Ishmael. “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” They sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem to the Grecians, the white people united under Alexander, and took “my silver and my gold” into their temples. God returns their recompense on their own head, and so they come over in chains, fall down and make supplication, “saying, Surely God is in thee; and there is none else, there is no God.”

The makers of idols “shall be ashamed, and also confounded”, but “Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation”, world without end. The word “world” means a group of people with common goals or interests, like the sports world or basketball world, so “world without end” and God so loved the world are not speaking of everybody but of Israel.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain, for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
precepts.point: There is no God else beside me, a just God and a Saviour; look unto me and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth, for God scattered us to the ends of the earth. I have sworn by myself that unto me every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear; in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified and shall glory.

note.label: Isaiah 45: I Form the Light and Create Darkness

precepts.why:
“I said not unto the seed of Jacob, Seek ye me in vain: I the Lord speak righteousness, I declare things that are right.” The Most High does not deal in vain, and he commands the same of his name: “Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.”

The Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain. He did not tell the seed of Jacob to seek him in vain, and he will not have his name taken in vain. As Paul said, we are not fighting like one that beateth the air; there is a reason. He created the earth not in vain but formed it to be inhabited, he made us the ones to rule over it, and it will go back to being like that.

precepts.text: The Lord shall scatter thee among all people, and there thou shalt serve other gods of wood and stone; two of the false religions we were cursed into serving are Christianity and Islam, gods our fathers never knew.
precepts.point: There is no God else beside me, a just God and a Saviour; look unto me and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth, for God scattered us to the ends of the earth. I have sworn by myself that unto me every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear; in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified and shall glory.

note.label: Isaiah 45: I Form the Light and Create Darkness

precepts.why:
“Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else.” Why the ends of the earth? Because God scattered us there: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

The Lord scattered us among all people, from one end of the earth to the other, and there we serve other gods of wood and stone that our fathers never knew. Two of the false religions we were cursed into serving are Christianity and Islam, gods our fathers never knew. That is who is told, “Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, ye that are escaped of the nations”, the ones with “no knowledge that set up the wood of their graven image, and pray unto a god that cannot save.” Come out from among them and be separate, touch not the unclean thing, and I will receive you: look unto him from the ends of the earth and be saved, for “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

precepts.text: The Lord forms the light and creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil; the Lord does all these things.
precepts.point: Shall a trumpet be blown in the city and the people not be afraid? Shall there be evil in a city and the Lord has not done it? The Most High is doing all these things; in Christianity we attribute anything bad to the devil, but the Lord says he does it.

note.label: Amos 3: You Only Have I Known

precepts.why:
“shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The Most High is doing all these things. In Christianity we attribute anything bad to the devil, but the Lord says he does it: “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things.”

The trumpet blown in the city and the evil in the city are the Lord's doing, not the devil's.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have called thee by thy name; the strangers were the elect according to the foreknowledge.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Who is the elect Peter wrote to? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” Israel is the elect.

So the strangers scattered through Pontus, Asia and the rest, elect according to the foreknowledge, are Israel, and the strangers of Rome standing in Jerusalem at Pentecost are Israel too. They had been surnamed, called by other names in other men's lands, though they did not know him, and now they heard the wonderful works of God in their own tongues.

precepts.text: The "many" is defined: "In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified," so the many that are justified are all the seed of Israel, not all nations.
precepts.point: If you claim Christ suffered and died for all nations, prove it "by the mouth of all his prophets." Show it through Isaiah, Ezekiel, Jeremiah, or Haggai, that Christ suffered and died for all nations, because the text says all his prophets foretold it.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Isaiah 53 says the righteous servant would justify many. Isaiah 45 defines the many: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

The many that are justified are all the seed of Israel, not all nations. That is what the prophets said Christ would suffer for, and Peter is preaching that fulfilled suffering to the brethren, the men of Israel who did it through ignorance.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” It was prophesied that the seed of Israel would be justified in the Lord, not by the blood of bulls and goats.

That is Galatians 2:16: “even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ.” The seed of Israel is justified in the Lord.

precepts.why: Who is the elect the angels are gathering? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect,” So the elect that the angels are gathering are only the Israelites. So please tell the people in the churches, in Creflo Dollar's church and TD Jakes's, God ain't coming to save you; he is only coming for the Israelites. That is what the Bible says. You can throw your money around at TD, Creflo, Juanita Bynum and whoever the hell, Benny Hinn: you ain't getting saved, brother or sister that's following them. They say I'm non-denominational, anybody can come. The Bible says the Lord is looking for the elect, and the elect is Israel. If you ain't coming that way, you ain't coming. Don't say you never was warned; you was warned.
